title: EFE Robot MCP tools, v1
description: One tool per agent-facing endpoint of the robot service (docs/protocol/eai-standard.md, "MCP tools"): the request fields and the reply as the service's client sends and receives them. GET /status has no tool (its fields come back in every reply's meta); GET /operations/<id> has none either (the server re-queries it itself when a reply is lost). schema.py narrows the list per task and drops each tool's `realtime_only` fields outside realtime mode. Every inputSchema is a self-contained draft 2020-12 object schema without $ref or top-level combinators.

tools.name: spec
tools.description: GET /spec: the robot's facts as the service gives them (action types with their layouts, limits and semantics, cameras, proprioception layout, budgets, timing). Saved whole as a JSON file (`spec_file`); also returned inline when it is small.

tools.name: observe
tools.description: POST /observe: what the robot's cameras and sensors have already recorded, returned at once: the current frame (`last_s` 0) or the last `last_s` seconds. It reads only; nothing moves and no time passes (standard mode: the world is frozen between submits). Fields left out take the service's defaults; any other field of this service's /observe goes in `fields`, sent as given. The reply comes back as the service's `meta` (unchanged) and its parts as files under /app/obs/: arrays as .npy (exact; load with numpy), each image also as .png (open it with your file-reading tool), video as .mp4. With `operation`, it instead waits for a call that answered `pending` (a call still running after 45 s returns {"pending": true, "operation": id}); nothing is sent.

cameras.description: camera names (realtime: [] = no images, only proprioception)

last_s.description: 0 (the default): the current frame; n: the last n seconds already recorded (at most the recorder's length in `spec`)

video.description: the service's video field (for example none, frames, mp4, both)

depth.description: the service's depth field, where it has one (for example "none", "last", "frames")

include_depth.description: the service's include_depth field, where it has one

fields.description: any other request field of this service (its spec / the client's docs), sent as given

inline_cameras.description: cameras whose last image is also returned in the result as a small image

operation.description: id of a pending call to wait for (nothing is sent)

tools.name: submit
tools.description: POST /submit, one step of the episode: rows of one of the robot's own action types (`spec` action_types: layout, units, limits), sent unchanged with these header fields. Standard mode: answers when the rows have run, with the chunk's video and its duration; nothing moves between submits. Realtime mode: answers at once with the chunk's duration and end step; the rows become the plan from control step `at` (default: the next one). To let time pass without new rows, send a hold chunk: `interpolate` "hold" and `seconds` n with no rows holds the target in force for n seconds of robot time (standard mode: it answers when they have run, with their video). Rows inline (`actions`) or, for long chunks, a file under /app (`actions_file`: .npy, .csv or a .json list of rows). The result's `step` repeats the reply's duration, end step, steps left and whether the episode is done; the reply comes back as the service's `meta` (unchanged) and its parts as files under /app/obs/: arrays as .npy (exact; load with numpy), each image also as .png (open it with your file-reading tool), video as .mp4.

actions_file.description: path under /app of the rows: .npy, .csv or .json

seconds.description: a hold chunk: with interpolate "hold" and no rows, hold the target in force for this many seconds of robot time

at.description: realtime mode: the control step the rows start at

depth.description: the service's depth field, where it has one

fields.description: any other request field of this service (its spec / the client's docs), sent as given

inline_cameras.description: cameras whose last image is also returned in the result as a small image

tools.name: reset
tools.description: POST /reset: abandon the running episode and start a new one from the same starting state; it uses one reset of the task's budget (`spec` budget.reset). The reply comes back as the service's `meta` (unchanged) and its parts as files under /app/obs/: arrays as .npy (exact; load with numpy), each image also as .png (open it with your file-reading tool), video as .mp4.

depth.description: the service's depth field, where it has one

fields.description: any other request field of this service (its spec / the client's docs), sent as given

inline_cameras.description: cameras whose last image is also returned in the result as a small image

tools.name: kinematics
tools.description: POST /kinematics with this JSON body: forward or inverse kinematics on the robot's own model (`spec` kinematics says what it takes). Never moves the robot; no robot time passes.

tools.name: finish
tools.description: POST /finish: end the episode now, in a task whose episode you end yourself (`spec` success_signal starting with "hidden"); after it every action is refused. In a task whose episode ends by itself the tool says so and sends nothing.
